@YvesNixVideographer ❤️ 32
The final scene in T2, where the T-800 lowers himself into the molten steel, seems to contain some interesting digital compositing work that was quite innovative for its time. You can see Arnold being lowered down on a cable, presumably shot in front of a bluescreen, with separate elements such as fire and smoke composited into the shot. The cgi work that comes just before this, showing the T-1000 after it has fallen into the molten steel, is also worth discussing. I remember reading somewhere that this scene was originally intended to be much more elaborate, but that due to the lack of time, it ultimately had to be rushed. I believe some of the animation was done by Steve “Spaz” Williams. The very last shot, where you see the T-1000’s face lying in the molten steel before it entirely starts falling apart into a liquid, apparently had to be rendered very quickly because of the time pressure. If I remember correctly, that shot was rendered at only 320 × 240 resolution. Using some kind of sharpening and upscaling techniques, they were apparently able to bring the footage up to something like 2K, allowing it to look convincing enough on the big screen. Please discuss this :)
